policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads the singular 'Keep thy foot', matching the qere singular רַגְלְךָ. The ketiv רגליך is plural ('thy feet'), which the English would have shown; the number is visible in the ASV wording, so the reading is distinguished.

Qere הוא and ketiv היא differ only in the gender of the pronoun, which English does not mark here; 'the king himself is served by the field' renders either. The only note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns English wording, so it cannot decide a reading. Base fallback carries the projection.

Qere רְאוּת and ketiv ראית are orthographic variants of the same noun of seeing; 'the beholding of them with his eyes' renders either identically. No ASV note is mapped to this unit, so nothing in the English distinguishes them.

Qere חַיָּיו and ketiv חיו are plene and defective spellings of the same phrase 'his life'; ASV 'all the days of his life' renders either. The two notes are classed alternative_rendering and hebrew_gloss, neither of which decides a reading.
